name: Tanigawadake by the Tenjin ridge (谷川岳)
region: Joshinetsu Kogen National Park, Gunma-Niigata border
why: A ropeway lifts you to 1,320 m, then an open ridge with chains and boardwalks leads to the two rock summits, the 'ears', above some of the steepest cliffs in Japan.
book: No permit. Joetsu Shinkansen to Jomo-Kogen, bus to the Tanigawadake Ropeway (about 50 minutes), ropeway to Tenjindaira (about 10 minutes); a chairlift goes on to Tenjin-toge. Check the time of the last ropeway down: there is no other easy way off.
water: None on the ridge: carry 1.5 litres. Drinks at Tenjindaira and at Kata-no-koya hut below the summit.
dangers: Chained rock steps on the ridge: slippery when wet and crowded on autumn weekends.
The weather changes fast between the Sea of Japan and Pacific sides: fog, wind and cold rain on the ridge even in summer.
Stay on the Tenjin ridge trail: the cliffs of Ichinokurazawa below the summits are climbing terrain where many people have died.
Snow on the ridge until June and from November.
turnaround: Not at Kumaanazawa shelter by 10:30, or the ridge in fog and wind: go back to Tenjindaira.

points.name: Tenjindaira
points.note: The top ropeway station at about 1,320 m. Take the traverse path west under the chairlift to the ridge (or ride the lift to Tenjin-toge).

points.name: Kumaanazawa shelter
points.note: A small emergency hut on the ridge. Above it the path climbs rock steps with chains, then a long flat ridge on boardwalks.

points.name: Kata-no-koya hut
points.note: The hut on the shoulder after the big scree slope, a few minutes below the first summit. Drinks and a roof in bad weather.

points.name: Tanigawadake twin summits
points.note: Toma-no-mimi, 1,963 m, then Oki-no-mimi, 1,977 m, 10 minutes on along the ridge. The east face drops straight to Ichinokurazawa. Back the same way.
